what_it_does: This paper describes a new type of oscillator—a circuit that generates very high-frequency radio signals in the terahertz range (around 224 gigahertz, well beyond WiFi and cellphone bands). The challenge is that conventional designs use small variable capacitors called varactors to tune the frequency, but varactors don't work well at these extreme frequencies and can't change the frequency much. Instead, this design uses switched inductors—elements that add or remove coils from the circuit—to achieve a wider tuning range (19.9%) while maintaining high signal quality. The innovation is combining these switch-controlled coils in a special resonator structure that works reliably at frequencies where previous approaches fail.
